chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

'The dog of the Magian — do not eat its prey, except if a Muslim takes it, trains it, and sends it (to hunt). And similarly is the falcon. And the dogs of the Ahl al-Dhimma and their falcons — it is permissible for Muslims to eat their prey.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الذِّمَّةِ: Ahl al-Dhimma — non-Muslim communities (primarily Jews, Christians, and Magians) living under a formal covenant of protection within an Islamic state
key_terms.الْبَازِي: Falcon — a trained bird of prey used in hunting
key_terms.الْمَجُوسِيُّ: Magian — a follower of Zoroastrianism (fire worship), treated distinctly in Islamic law from People of the Book
key_terms.حَلَال: Halal — permissible according to Islamic law
key_terms.صَيْد: Prey/game — animals hunted by trained animals for consumption

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible (halal) to eat prey caught by a dog or falcon belonging to a Magian or non-Muslim according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a jurisprudential ruling concerning hunting animals owned by non-Muslims, specifically distinguishing between two categories: the Magians (Zoroastrians) and the Ahl al-Dhimma (non-Muslim protected subjects under Islamic governance). The prey of a Magian's hunting dog is not permissible unless a Muslim acquires, re-trains, and dispatches the dog, whereas the prey of hunting animals belonging to Ahl al-Dhimma is permissible outright for Muslims. This ruling reflects classical Shia jurisprudential distinctions regarding ritual permissibility based on the legal status of the non-Muslim owner.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A dog of the Magians, do not eat its prey, except if the Muslim takes it, so he trains it and sends it (to hunt); and similar to that is the falcon, and a dog of the Ahl Al-Zimma (People under the responsibility), and their falcons are Permissible for the Muslims that they should be eating their prey’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Do not use for food what the dog of a Zoroastrian person hunts, unless a Muslim has taken it to train and sends it to hunt. This applies to what the dogs of taxpayers and their falcons hunt, thus, it is lawful for the Muslims to use for food.’”
